alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The white pulp of the spleen consists of diffuse (T-dependent) and nodular (B-dependent) lymphoid tissues that surround arterioles after they leave trabeculae. The diffuse tissue forms a sleeve around each arteriole. The lymphoid nodules are suspended within the diffuse areas. The surrounding red pulp consists of splenic cords and sinuses.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Primary lymphoid nodules are clusters of lymphoid cells located as solitary nodules in the lamina propria of tubular organs (as here) and as aggregates in tonsils and Peyer’s patches. A primary lymphoid nodule consist mostly of small lymphocytes aggregated in the lamina propria and filter tissue fluid. The absence of a pale, germinal center distinguishes this primary nodule from a secondary nodule.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Like the lymph node, the spleen is entirely encapsulated; however, in the spleen, connective tissue trabeculae extend farther into the organ than do those of the lymph node. In lymph nodes, lymphoid nodules are confined to the cortex; lymphoid nodules in the spleen are present throughout the organ, forming part of the white pulp.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Spleen is differentiated from lymph node and thymus because it lacks the cortex and medulla these organs possess. Lymphoid nodules, part of white pulp, are scattered throughout the spleen; their distinguishing feature is their central arteriole, which is displaced toward the margin when a nodule develops within the PALS surrounding the arteriole.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The inner region of the lymph node cortex, the paracortex, is a T-dependent area. It lies just beneath the superficial cortex where the lymphoid nodules are located. Beneath the paracortex is the medulla. Under antigenic stimulation, T cells in this region become activated, replicate and leave the lymph node via the efferent lymphatic vessels. These T cells are then returned to the blood and carried to peripheral sites throughout the body.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this germinal center, macrophages (tingible body macrophages) with phagosomes in their cytoplasm, indicate the phagocytic activity occurring in this region. These macrophages are phagocytosing apoptotic cells in various stages of degradation that occurs during immune selection. The term “tangible” refers to the fact that the phagocytosed material is stainable, mostly condensed chromatin fragments.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The splenic sinuses are venous sinuses and hence are lined by endothelial cells. However, these cells are unique, having large nuclei that bulge into the lumen of the sinusoid. Additionally, these cells are extremely long, with their longitudinal axes oriented parallel to the flow of blood in the sinus.
